text:
Fixed. Bug in `src/interval.js` → `Interval.fromISO`: it called `DateTime.fromISO` on both halves of the string unconditionally and only then checked `.isValid`. With `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true`, parsing a perfectly valid interval like `2007-03-01T13:00:00/P1Y2M10DT2H30M` threw an `InvalidDateTimeError` (because the duration half isn't a DateTime) instead of falling back to `Duration.fromISO`.

The fix wraps each `DateTime.fromISO` call in try/catch and tracks `startIsValid`/`endIsValid`, so a DateTime parse failure falls through to the Duration parsing path as intended (and a genuinely unparsable input still ends in `Interval.invalid(...)`, which throws under `throwOnInvalid`).

Verified: a reproduction of `Interval.fromISO works with Settings.throwOnInvalid` (valid date/date, date/duration and duration/date inputs must not throw) now passes; the full `test/interval` suite passes (127 tests); the whole suite is unchanged at 892 passed with only the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures that were already failing before my edit. ESLint and Prettier are clean.

Fixed. Bug in `src/impl/util.js` → `objToLocalTS`. It built the timestamp with `Date.UTC(...)` (which maps years 0–99 to 19XX) and then "reverted" the year with `setUTCFullYear(year - 1900)`. That revert is only exact while the day/month doesn't overflow: when the day overflows past a February, the shifted year (e.g. 1999→2000, which has a Feb 29) and the target year (0099→0100, which has no Feb 29) disagree by one day, so `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 62 })` returned 0100-03-02 instead of 0100-03-03.

Fix: compute the timestamp for the year shifted 400 years forward (the Gregorian calendar repeats exactly every 400 years, so the calendar including any overflowed days/months is identical) and then subtract those 400 years (146097 days) from the timestamp. Valid dates in years 0–99 are unchanged; only the previously wrong overflow cases change.

Verified with a brute-force check of `plus({days})`/`minus({days})` for every month of every year 0–105 with day offsets 1…1000 against a plain-Date reference: 0 mismatches (previously 43200 mismatches). The existing `DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier` test still passes and the full suite is unchanged at 892 passed with only the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.

In progress: the root cause in `src/datetime.js` is identified (the 1974 year-round-DST offsets are computed wrongly for most dates); a fix is being written and verified against a day-by-day 1974 check plus the full suite. ETA ~5 min.
In progress: `src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js` is being fixed so that a non-numeric offset yields an invalid zone (and hence an invalid DateTime). ETA ~5 min.

Fixed. Bug in `src/duration.js`: three entries were missing from the unit-conversion matrices, so those conversions returned `undefined`/NaN (surfacing as 0):
- `casualMatrix.years.quarters` (should be 4)
- `casualMatrix.quarters.seconds` (should be 91 * 24 * 60 * 60)
- `accurateMatrix.years.quarters` (should be 4)

Consequences: `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).as("years")`, `{ years: 1 }.as("quarters")`, `{ quarters: 1 }.as("seconds")` (and the reverse directions) all returned 0 instead of the correct value, in both `casual` and `longterm` conversion accuracy.

Fix: added the three missing entries. Verified by checking all 72 ordered unit pairs × both accuracies against the mathematical unit definitions (1 y = 4 q = 12 mo = 52 wk = 365 d casual / 365.2425 d longterm; 1 q = 3 mo = 13 wk = 91 d; 1 mo = 4 wk = 30 d; 1 wk = 7 d; 1 d = 24 h; 1 h = 60 min; 1 min = 60 s; 1 s = 1000 ms) plus `shiftTo`/`normalize` round trips — all finite, positive and correct. Full suite unchanged at 892 passed with only the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.

Fixed. Bug in `src/datetime.js` → `get isInDST()`. It decided DST by comparing the current offset with `this.set({ month: 1 }).offset` (and `{ month: 5 }`). `set({month: 1})` keeps the day of month, so for 1974 — when the USA was on year-round DST from Jan 6 to Oct 27 — a date like 1974-01-07 produced a *January* reference date that is itself in DST (offset -240), so `-240 > -240` was false and `isInDST` wrongly returned false for most of the year.

Fix: compare against the start of the year instead of the same day in January:
```js
this.offset > this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 }).offset ||
this.offset > this.set({ month: 5 }).offset
```
Now the January reference is always a standard-time date, so every date in the 1974 DST window (Jan 6 02:00 through Oct 27 1974) reports `isInDST === true`, and dates before Jan 6 / after Oct 27 report false.

Verified with a day-by-day sweep of all of 1974 in America/New_York (isInDST matches the Jan 6–Oct 27 window; the only edge is Jan 6 at exactly 00:00, which is still EST before the 02:00 transition) plus the existing DST tests. Full suite unchanged at 892 passed with only the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.

Fixed. Bug in `src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js`: `get isValid()` was hard-coded to `return true`, so a FixedOffsetZone built from a non-numeric offset (e.g. `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp")`, or `DateTime.local().setZone("UTC+blorp")`) claimed to be valid and DateTimes created in it were considered valid too.

Fix: `get isValid() { return isNumber(this.fixed); }` (with `isNumber` imported from `../impl/util.js`).

Verified: `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp").isValid === false`, `FixedOffsetZone.instance(60).isValid === true`, `DateTime.fromObject({ year: 2020, month: 1, day: 1, zone: FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp") }).isValid === false`, `DateTime.local().setZone("UTC+blorp").isValid === false`, while valid offsets still work (`DateTime.fromISO("2020-01-01T00:00:00+05:30", { setZone: true }).offset === 330`). Full suite unchanged at 892 passed with only the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.
